subject: Agriculture
title: Farmers vs. Cities
description: A quick, practical guide to Farmers vs. Cities.

hook.text: As cities grow, they need more water. The easiest source? Buy it from nearby farms.

buildup.text: Urban areas offer farmers top dollar for water rights. A farmer's water can be worth more than the crops.

discovery.text: Las Vegas pays farmers to fallow fields and transfer water. It's cheaper than building new reservoirs.

twist.text: When farms sell water rights, rural communities lose jobs, tax revenue, and their economic base.

climax.text: The tension between feeding people and quenching cities is growing as both populations and droughts increase.

punchline.text: Water flows toward money. Farms often lose.

quiz.question: Why do cities buy water rights from farmers?
options: It's often cheaper than building new water infrastructure
